title: Potato Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Potato Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Potato nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in patatas, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Potato nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your patatas (potato) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium, calcium, boron, sulfur and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Potato leaves with brown, scorched, curled edges from potassium shortage
heroImage.credit: Simranpreetsidhu, CC BY SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium, boron, sulfur and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which potato nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a potato nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest potato nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in potato

Leaves turn evenly yellow, veins and all, starting on the older leaves. When nitrogen is given, young leaves green up but the old ones stay yellow. Severe shortage makes leaves cup upward, and the crop stops early with small tubers. You see it most at this stage: before and during tuber set.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in patatas
Sandy soils, heavy rain that washes nitrogen out, and too little fertilizer in highland fields cropped every season.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency also yellows the whole plant but includes the young leaves and gives a reddish tint to veins. Magnesium deficiency yellows between green veins. To be sure, check that the yellowing started on the old leaves, then test the soil. A leaf tissue test confirms it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 following the soil test, hilled in beside the rows. Give a urea spray of 10 g per liter (160 g in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days for quick help. A usual side dress is 1 to 2 bags of Urea 46 0 0 or 2 to 4 bags of Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 per hectare, 30 to 45 days after planting.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Ammonium Chloride** by La Filipina (25 0 0), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, split nitrogen between planting and hilling, and add compost.
Potassium deficiency in potato

blocks.alt: Potato leaves with brown, scorched, curled edges from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Simranpreetsidhu, CC BY SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Leaflets crinkle, the tips burn and dead tissue spreads between the veins while the veins stay green. Leaves curl and look scorched, with dark edges. The yellowing does not reverse even after potash is given, and tubers stay small. You see it most at this stage: tuber bulking.
Why potassium deficiency happens in patatas
Sandy and acid soils, and fields cropped for years without potash. Potato needs a higher soil potassium level than most field crops.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency can look much the same when advanced, but starts as mottled yellow between veins. Early blight gives round spots with rings. To be sure, soil test for potassium (aim higher than for field crops) and a leaf test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test, split between planting and hilling. For quick help spray potassium sulfate at 10 g per liter (160 g in a 16 liter sprayer) in the morning. A usual dose is 2 to 3 bags of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 per hectare, half at planting and half when the roots or tubers start to swell.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep the soil pH above 6 with lime or dolomite, add organic matter and wood ash, and give potash every crop.
Phosphorus deficiency in potato

Plants grow slowly and stay stunted and darker than normal. Stems, leaf stalks and the undersides of leaves turn purple, and the lower leaf surface looks grey green. Older leaves get dead spots and leaflets curl upward. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in patatas
Acid and volcanic soils that lock up phosphorus, and cold soil early in the season.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency also curls leaflets but burns the tips and edges. Purple top viruses give purple and rolled top leaves, not dark plants. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus (potato needs a higher level than field crops).
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and bone meal or rock phosphate for the long term, following the soil test. Phosphorus is taken up best at pH 6.2 to 7.0. Band it near the seed pieces at planting. A usual basal dose is 4 to 6 bags of Complete 14 14 14 per hectare in the furrow at planting.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, apply phosphorus at planting each crop and lime acid soils.
Magnesium deficiency in potato

blocks.alt: Potato leaves yellow between the veins with brown dead patches from magnesium shortage (small credit line in corner)
blocks.caption: Photo: ScotGov SASA, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Mottled yellow areas form between the veins, first on young mature leaves. In advanced cases dead tissue between the veins gives a scorched look that can resemble potassium deficiency. You see it most at this stage: mid season.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in patatas
Acid, sandy soils in rainy highlands, and heavy potash.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency starts with burned tips and crinkled leaflets. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and pH, and a leaf test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Give about 80 kg magnesium sulfate per hectare in bands near the plants. Apply it apart from potash. Use Dolomite on acid soils over the long run. Put the soil dose in before planting or when the rains begin. Sprays show results in 10 to 14 days.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid fields with dolomite instead of plain lime. Test the soil every two or three years.
Calcium deficiency in potato

Young leaves and leaflet tips turn pale, stay small and curl slightly. Severe cases stunt the plant. Sprout tips can turn black and die, and tubers show rusty brown spots inside. You see it most at this stage: tuber bulking, and in stored seed potatoes as they sprout.
Why calcium deficiency happens in patatas

Very acid soils, and also higher pH sandy soils, where potatoes may respond well to added calcium. High phosphorus and boron shortage make it worse. Heavy potash or ammonium fertilizer, salty soil and dry spells keep calcium from reaching fruit and young leaves.
How to tell it apart

Boron deficiency also kills the growing point and gives brittle leaves. A leaf test does not show tuber calcium, since calcium may reach the leaves but not the tubers. To be sure, soil pH and calcium test. Cut tubers to look for internal spots. A soil test for calcium and pH, and a leaf test, confirm it.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

On acid soils, lime about 250 kg per hectare where the pH is 5.5 to 6. About 840 kg per hectare in two splits where it is 3.5 to 4.5. On alkaline soils, or to add calcium without raising pH, use Gypsum.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** (36.2 percent calcium), **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium) and **Philphos Gypsum** (22.2 percent calcium and 17.4 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test the soil before each crop and keep the soil evenly moist so calcium can move into the tubers. Keep potash in balance with magnesium and calcium.
Boron deficiency in potato

Leaves pale slightly. The growing tip dies, so the plant loses its main shoot and grows in a bushy rosette. Leaves turn brittle and break easily, and young leaves droop even though the soil is still wet. You see it most at this stage: mid season.
Why boron deficiency happens in patatas
Sandy soils low in organic matter, high pH soils and dry spells.
How to tell it apart
Calcium deficiency looks very similar. A soil or leaf test separates them. To be sure, soil test for boron. In a soil test, less than 0.5 ppm of boron is low.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Give about 10 kg Borax per hectare to the soil, or a borax spray of 1 g per liter (16 g in a 16 liter sprayer). Keep boron apart from calcium and ammonium fertilizers. Give boron before flowering: flowers and fruit set need it most.

Sold here with boron: **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl Chem (11 percent boron), **Fertibagra 15G** by Unilox Far East Resources (14.6 percent boron), **B17 (Boric Acid)** by Newman Chemicals (17 percent boron) and **Better Yield** by Bacphil Planters Fertilizer (0 0 0.9 with 10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test for boron before planting on sandy fields. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Sulfur deficiency in potato

The whole plant yellows evenly, young leaves included, with a reddish tint in the veins, leaf stalks and leaf undersides. In advanced cases leaves stand upright, twist and turn brittle. You see it most at this stage: early to mid growth.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in patatas
Soils low in organic matter, sulfur free fertilizer for years, and burning crop waste.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency starts on the old leaves and has no red veins. To be sure, soil and leaf test for sulfur. In a soil test, less than 10 ppm of sulfate sulfur is low.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency

Use a sulfur bearing fertilizer such as Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or single superphosphate. Give about 25 kg sulfur dust per hectare on sulfur poor soils, or Gypsum on alkaline soils. Give it at planting or with the first side dress.

Sold here with sulfur: **Atlas Ammosul 21 0 0** by Atlas Fertilizer (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur), **Philphos Gypsum** (22.2 percent calcium and 17.4 percent sulfur), **Harvester Sulphate of Potash** by Universal Harvester (0 0 50 with 17.5 percent sulfur) and **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add organic matter and use a fertilizer that carries sulfur. Test the soil every two or three years.
Zinc deficiency in potato

Young leaves yellow and mature leaves show small pits on the upper surface between the veins. Dead patches between the veins spread while the main veins stay green. You see it most at this stage: early to mid growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in patatas
High pH soils, heavy phosphorus, and soils low in zinc. Potato has a medium zinc need.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium deficiency yellows between veins on older leaves without pitting. To be sure, soil and leaf test for zinc. In a soil test, less than 0.8 ppm of zinc is low.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Give about 20 kg Zinc sulfate per hectare to the soil, or in severe cases a morning spray of 2 g zinc sulfate with 2.5 g lime per liter. Keep zinc and phosphate applications apart. Give the soil dose at planting or when the rains begin, and sprays on young growth.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Petbowe Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** (33 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc) and **Liquid Chelate Zinc with Sulfur** by Sagrex (10 percent zinc and 5 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep soil pH between 5 and 7.5 and test for zinc. Test the soil every two or three years.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any potato nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your patatas needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Potato nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my patatas leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: whole leaves, veins included, turn evenly pale yellow, starting low on the plant. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at sulfur deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in potato?
items.a: Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 following the soil test, hilled in beside the rows. Give a urea spray of 10 g per liter (160 g in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days for quick help.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in potato?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test, split between planting and hilling. For quick help spray potassium sulfate at 10 g per liter (160 g in a 16 liter sprayer) in the morning.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in potato?
items.a: Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and bone meal or rock phosphate for the long term, following the soil test. Phosphorus is taken up best at pH 6.2 to 7.0.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my patatas lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the potato nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
